overview.title: 📖 Overview: Individual Offerings, Communal Offerings, and a Digression on Writing
overview.subtitle: Temurah 14a–14b
overview.hebrewSource: קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, וְאֵין קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: A new mishna catalogs the structural differences between offerings brought by an individual and those brought by the community: individual offerings generate temurah, may be male or female, and must be replaced if missed; communal offerings do neither, but override Shabbat and impurity if their time is fixed (Rabbi Meir refines this last point). The Gemara tests each general statement against counter-examples — birds, offspring, substitutes, and various offering-types restricted to one sex — resolving each by reading the mishna's claims narrowly. A discussion of when 'missed' communal offerings and their libations may still be brought triggers a lengthy digression on whether halakha may ever be written down, before the daf returns to carefully parsing Numbers 29:39, phrase by phrase, to identify which offerings each clause is teaching about — including a story about Avshalom's nazirite vow.

slides.title: ⚖️ New Mishna: Individual vs. Communal Offerings
slides.subtitle: Each type has powers the other lacks
rows: Yes — owner is liable to bring it later
No — the day passes and it's gone (but libations already begun must still be completed)

callout.label: Rabbi Meir's refinement:
callout.text: The real distinction isn't individual vs. communal at all — it's whether the offering's TIME is fixed. The High Priest's daily griddle-cakes and the Yom Kippur bull are individual offerings, yet they too override Shabbat and impurity.

slides.title: 🐦 Does EVERY Individual Offering Make Temurah?
slides.subtitle: The Gemara tests the mishna's opening claim against three exceptions

nodes.content: ❓ Birds are individual offerings, yet they never make temurah!
💬 Answer: the mishna means only animal offerings, not birds
❓ An offspring is an individual offering, yet (per the Rabbis) it doesn't make temurah!
💬 Answer: this mishna follows Rabbi Yehuda, who holds offspring DOES make temurah
❓ A substitute itself is an individual offering, yet it can't generate a further substitute!
✅ Final answer: the mishna refers only to the PRIMARY offering — now even the Rabbis' view works too

callout.label: Method:
callout.text: Each challenge narrows the mishna's scope rather than overturning it — a pattern seen throughout the tractate.

slides.title: ♀️♂️ Does EVERY Individual Offering Allow Both Sexes?
slides.subtitle: Counter-examples and how each is reconciled
rows: Only male animals allowed — never female
There IS a female option: the bird burnt offering, which has no male/unblemished requirement
Only female animals allowed — never male
There IS a male option: the king's goat sin offering (שְׂעִיר נָשִׂיא)
Only male allowed, and no communal parallel exists
The mishna's rule applies only to offerings shared by both individuals AND the community — guilt offering has no communal form
The mishna means only SOME individual offerings (e.g., peace offerings) allow either sex — not a universal rule

callout.label: Recurring lesson:
callout.text: Broad mishnaic statements in this tractate consistently turn out to describe the typical case, not an exceptionless rule.

slides.title: ✍️ Can Oral Torah Be Written Down?
slides.subtitle: A digression sparked by a debate over sending halakha in a letter
slides.label: The story:
slides.text: Rav Dimi wanted to send Rav Yosef a ruling about libations in a letter, but the Gemara objects: Rabbi Yoḥanan taught that 'those who write down halakhot are like those who burn the Torah' — the Oral Law must stay oral, just as the Written Law must stay written (derived from Exodus 34:27, and from the school of Rabbi Yishmael's reading of 'these words'). Yet the Gemara notes that Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish themselves read from a written scroll of aggada on Shabbat, justified by the verse 'It is time to act for the Lord — they have violated Your Torah' (Psalms 119:126): sometimes one rule must yield so the Torah as a whole is not forgotten. New material, in particular, may need to be written down precisely because memory alone cannot preserve it.

slides.title: 📜 Parsing Numbers 29:39, Phrase by Phrase
slides.subtitle: Rav Dimi (citing Rabbi Yoḥanan) matches each clause to a distinct category of offering

steps.content: 1️⃣ 'These you shall offer... in your appointed seasons' — the OBLIGATORY Festival offerings (appearance, Festival, additional)
2️⃣ 'Beside your vows and voluntary offerings' — teaches these may be sacrificed on the intermediate days (chol hamoed)
3️⃣ 'And your burnt offerings' (not already covered) — must mean the new mother's and the leper's burnt offerings
4️⃣ 'And your meal offerings' (not already covered) — must mean the sota's meal offering of jealousy

5️⃣ 'And your libations and peace offerings' — libations follow peace offerings: day only; 'peace offerings' includes the NAZIRITE's peace offering (Abaye argues it should instead mean the Paschal-overflow peace offering)

callout.label: Resolved via Avshalom:
callout.text: Abaye's challenge about whether a nazirite offering counts as 'vowed/voluntary' is settled by identifying Avshalom's Hebron trip (II Samuel 15:7-8) as fulfilling a genuine nazirite vow — private altars were then still permitted, so he could sacrifice anywhere he chose.

summary.principle: Individual offerings generate temurah, allow either sex, and must be replaced if missed, while communal offerings do the opposite but override Shabbat and impurity when time-fixed — though nearly every clause of the mishna turns out to describe the common case rather than an absolute rule.

flowSteps.content: ⚖️ Mishna: individual offerings make temurah, both sexes, must be replaced; communal offerings override Shabbat/impurity
🐦 Exceptions (birds, offspring, substitutes) each narrow the mishna's true scope

columns.content: ♀️♂️ Male/female claim likewise narrowed via bird olah, king's goat, etc.
✍️ Detour: is writing down halakha ever permitted? Sometimes, for the Torah's survival

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: broad mishnaic rules in this tractate consistently describe the typical case, refined by careful reading

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Meir's refinement of the new mishna, what actually determines whether an offering overrides Shabbat and ritual impurity?
o: Whether it is an individual or communal offering
Whether its time is fixed, regardless of whether it is individual or communal
Whether it is male or female
Whether it generates temurah
quiz.e: Rabbi Meir notes that the High Priest's griddle-cakes and the Yom Kippur bull are individual offerings that DO override Shabbat and impurity, proving the real criterion is a fixed time, not individual-vs-communal status.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara reconcile the fact that a substitute animal is an individual offering, yet cannot itself generate a further substitute?
o: It says the mishna is simply incorrect
It explains the mishna's rule about individual offerings applies only to the PRIMARY offering, not to a substitute
It says substitutes are actually communal offerings
It cites Rabbi Yehuda as the sole authority
quiz.e: The Gemara narrows the mishna's claim to primary offerings only, which also allows even the Rabbis' view (that offspring don't make temurah) to be reconciled with the mishna.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara resolve the apparent contradiction that a burnt offering (olah) is an individual offering but comes only as a male?
o: It says burnt offerings don't really exist
It points to the bird burnt offering, which has no male/unblemished requirement and can be female
It claims the mishna is wrong
It says burnt offerings are actually communal
quiz.e: The Gemara notes that while an animal burnt offering must be male, a bird burnt offering carries no such requirement, satisfying the mishna's broader claim that individual offerings may be male or female.

quiz.q: According to the digression on writing down halakha, what is the general prohibition, and what exception is noted?
o: Writing is always forbidden with no exceptions
Oral Torah generally may not be written down (like burning Torah), but new material may need to be written so it isn't forgotten, per 'it is time to act for the Lord'
Only Written Torah may never be written down
There is no prohibition at all
quiz.e: Rabbi Yoḥanan's principle likens writing down halakha to burning Torah, but the Gemara notes an exception: new material may be written to prevent it from being forgotten, based on Psalms 119:126.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara's reading of Numbers 29:39, what does the phrase 'and your meal offerings' (not already covered by vows/gifts) refer to?
o: The meal offering brought with a burnt offering
The meal offering of the sota (the meal offering of jealousy)
The daily meal offering in the Temple
The meal offering of a nazirite
quiz.e: Since vow and voluntary meal offerings are already covered by earlier clauses, the Gemara concludes this phrase must refer to the sota's meal offering of jealousy, an obligatory offering not otherwise mentioned.
